title: Five layouts for the run report
brief: Zach: keep 3D on the left and the question tabs on the right, keep the content, rethink the layout. Five complete redesigns on the same real page (JTC diagnostics, X1.ElbowStop@-60: Target, Command, Measured, MuJoCo truth; shoulder and elbow; 27 Diagnostics channels).
boundary: Runnable prototypes on traj_compare's own stack (vanilla JS, uPlot 1.6.30, three.js r160, vendored) and the real payload. Layout, time, charts, 3D, toggles and channel choosing are real; Open in Rerun shows the command instead of starting Rerun, there is no robot mesh (the payload has none), and the other scenario pages are not wired.
invariants: 3D view left, the six question tabs right
Same real X1.ElbowStop@-60 payload, 1600 × 1000, dark scheme
One time for 3D and every chart: play, step, scrub on any chart, Worst moment
All 27 channels, eye toggles, deg (default) / rad, Open in Rerun
Every panel boundary draggable and remembered; settings foldable

axes.name: How 27 channels are chosen
values: a lane per flag that fired + add-lane picker
every channel a strip, changed first

defaultWhy: Signal strips leads at 88/100 with Answer first one point behind (87): strips put every chart of a tab, and all 27 channels, on one screen under one aligned ruler, with each run's value at the playhead; Answer first is the calmer first read. Co-leaders: the recommendation is fragile.
decisionHinge: Whether a tab's first read should be one big chart (V1) or a table of small strips (V4). Moving 5 points from “One time across 3D and every chart” to “One answer first” makes Answer first lead 88 to 87; raising “Fits traj_compare” has the same effect, since V4 adds a new strip renderer. Splice candidate: V1's answer bar and changed-first Diagnostics list, V4's sticky ruler and strips, V2's run track headers with solo.

variants.name: Answer first
variants.thesis: Lead the page and every tab with a computed one-line answer and one chart; fold the rest, and put the time lane in a footer under both panels.
variants.bestWhen: Zach opens a report to learn the verdict and the one chart that shows it, and only sometimes digs into a second chart or channel.
variants.losesWhen: He wants to compare many charts at once: everything but the hero chart is one click away, and the footer lane's x does not line up with the charts.

decisions.label: Hierarchy
decisions.value: A page answer bar (verdict, facts, the flags that fired, Jump to the worst moment) over everything; each tab title carries its own answer badge.

decisions.label: Detail
decisions.value: Each tab opens on its answer line and one hero chart; “N more charts” and the statistics table fold under it.

decisions.label: Diagnostics
decisions.value: Changed channels first, grouped in plain words with first change and peak; click a row to open its charts in place; the 12 flat ones fold into one line.

decisions.label: Time
decisions.value: Today's lane as a resizable page footer under both panels.

variants.name: Editor timeline
variants.thesis: Make a video-editor dock the page's spine: ruler, a track per run, and a lane per diagnostic event that fired, so the story of the run reads left to right.
variants.bestWhen: The question is when things happened and in what order: collision, contact, blocked, path tolerance and settling are bars on one time axis, and event › steps through them.
variants.losesWhen: The dock takes a third of the height, so the charts above are short; continuous channels only show once added as a lane.

decisions.label: Time
decisions.value: A full-width, resizable dock: transport, ‹ event · Worst moment · event ›, ruler, run tracks, event lanes, waveform lanes.

decisions.label: Channels
decisions.value: Every flag that fired is already a lane (bars); “+ Add a lane” adds any of the 27 as a waveform; clicking a lane opens it in Diagnostics.

decisions.label: Runs
decisions.value: Track headers carry eye, solo, colour and the run's error at the playhead.

decisions.label: 3D settings
decisions.value: A 58 px edge toolbar whose buttons show their current value; each opens one slider.

variants.name: Inspector column
variants.thesis: Three panes: the 3D with its time lane under it, the question tab as a dense chart grid, and a foldable inspector that owns every setting and the channel list.
variants.bestWhen: A power user wants every chart at once and a single place for settings, like a CAD or IDE inspector.
variants.losesWhen: The middle pane is narrow: the tab bar scrolls, charts are small, and nothing says what the answer is beyond one bold line.

decisions.label: Composition
decisions.value: 3D + lane | tabs | inspector, each boundary draggable; the inspector folds to give charts the width.

decisions.label: Channels
decisions.value: Search box, “only changed” filter and grouped ticks; the ticked channels are what Diagnostics shows.

decisions.label: Runs
decisions.value: Inspector table: eye, solo, colour, error at the playhead, and a ◆ jump to each run's worst moment.

decisions.label: Time
decisions.value: The lane sits under the 3D: time and the picture belong together.

keepParts: run table with per-run worst jump

variants.name: Signal strips
variants.thesis: Start every chart as a 40 px strip (name, sparkline, each run's value at the playhead) under one sticky ruler, and open any strip into a full chart, so a tab reads like a table.
variants.bestWhen: Scanning many signals for the one that moved: all 27 channels and all eight raw signals fit one screen, and the playhead runs down every strip.
variants.losesWhen: A strip's shape is small and auto-scaled, so magnitudes are read from the numbers; a first-time reader may not know a strip opens.

decisions.label: Charts
decisions.value: Every chart starts folded as a strip; click its name to open it in place on the same x as the ruler.

decisions.label: Time
decisions.value: A sticky ruler + transport over the strips, aligned with every sparkline.

decisions.label: Runs
decisions.value: Run pills in the page header: eye, solo, colour, error at the playhead.

decisions.label: 3D settings
decisions.value: Three named looks (Clean · Ghost + comet · Error arrows) and a fine-tune drawer with the sliders.

keepParts: strips with values at the playhead

variants.name: Moment first
variants.thesis: Organise the page around “now”: it opens at the worst moment, a moment card says what is happening, events step the time, and channels are found by typing.
variants.bestWhen: Investigating one incident: the card names the event at the playhead, ‹ previous / next event › jumps between them, and “near this moment” suggests the channels that move there.
variants.losesWhen: The card and player bar sit on the 3D view, and finding a channel needs its name or a moment; there is no list of what changed over the run.

decisions.label: Entry
decisions.value: Opens at the worst moment; every tab leads with an “At this moment” readout of its signals per run.

decisions.label: Navigation
decisions.value: Question tabs as a vertical rail, each with its answer badge.

decisions.label: Channels
decisions.value: A command palette (press /), pinned channel chips, and suggestions that move within ±0.25 s of the playhead.

decisions.label: Time
decisions.value: A video-player bar on the 3D's bottom edge with event ticks; [ ] step events, 1–4 toggle runs.
